findings.description: The unattended --consumed-by path never checks that the map is handed-off, although the command explicitly limits this exception to handed-off maps.
findings.failure_mode: An unattended invocation against a charting map rejects its open ledger rows, closes its unresolved tickets and epic, and marks the map closed without completing the operator's decisions.
findings.suggested_fix: Before any mutation, require Status handed-off for --consumed-by, allowing an idempotent retry of an already consumed map.

findings.description: Comparing porcelain status text does not detect changes to files that were already dirty before the probe.
findings.failure_mode: If app/foo is already modified, a probe that overwrites its contents through an absolute path leaves the same ' M app/foo' status entry. The helper exits successfully despite modifying the main tree and potentially destroying the operator's uncommitted work.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare content fingerprints and file membership before and after the probe, including existing dirty and untracked files, or refuse dirty main trees and explicitly handle ignored files.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff version of .claude/agents/chart-researcher.md grants the subagent the Write tool and .claude/data/agent-types.yaml registers chart-researcher as write_capable: true. The only enforcement of the 'writes one file' rule is chart-ticket.sh research-end, whose baseline (the dispatch marker) and exempt directory are both grimoires/loa/research/.
findings.description: research-begin stores the scope baseline at grimoires/loa/research/.chart-<slug>-<ticket>.dispatch, and research-end exempts every path under grimoires/loa/research/ from the 'bad' diff (awk filter) while the 'newer' check compares mtimes against that same marker. A Write-capable researcher (the diff's tools list includes Write; the researcher is also fed untrusted WebFetch content by design) can Write any path in the repo, then rewrite the marker so it contains the post-state lines; comm -13 then yields nothing and no file is newer than the freshly written marker. It can also overwrite other maps' reports in the exempt directory. Separately, the P0 full-file copy of chart-researcher.md removes Write and says the session saves the final message, which contradicts both the diff and agent-types.yaml write_capable: true; one of the two is stale.
findings.failure_mode: A prompt-injected or misbehaving research subagent modifies files outside grimoires/loa/research/ (e.g. .claude/ settings, hooks, App-Zone code) and research-end reports a clean pass, defeating the one mechanical guard the skill relies on.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the marker outside the exempt tree (e.g. under ${G}/.chart-state/ or $TMPDIR with the path recorded in a non-writable location), make the exemption exact-match on the single expected report path rather than the whole research directory, and reconcile chart-researcher.md with agent-types.yaml (either drop Write and set write_capable: false, or keep Write and fix the scope check).

findings.description: op_close with --consumed-by skips the interactive-context check (by design, SDD D-4.5) but never verifies the map doc's Status is handed-off. .claude/commands/chart.md states the unattended exception applies 'on a handed-off map'. Nothing in op_close (or chart-guard.sh --close-consumed) enforces that, so a charting map with open tickets can be consumed unattended: every open ledger row is rejected with 'map closed: consumed by <cycle>', every question bead and the epic are closed, and Status becomes closed.
findings.failure_mode: An autonomous /plan-and-analyze run (or any unattended caller) names a map that is still being charted; its open decisions are rejected in the ledger and its beads closed, destroying an in-progress map without the operator present, which is exactly what the interactive-only rule exists to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: In op_close, when --consumed-by is given require doc_field Status == handed-off (and a context snapshot at grimoires/loa/context/chart-<slug>.md) and die otherwise; apply the same check in chart-guard.sh --close-consumed.

findings.cross_file_justification: chart-frontier.sh and chart-ticket.sh bead_row (both in this diff) read the bead type as (.issue_type // .type), while get-ready-work.sh reads only .issue_type. The same author treats the field name as uncertain in two scripts but not the third, and the third is the build-path boundary that /implement and implementing-tasks SKILL.md now depend on.
findings.description: The question-bead exclusion is select((.issue_type // "") != "question"). If br ready --json emits the type under 'type' (as the sibling scripts allow for), the field resolves to "" and no bead is ever dropped, so decision tickets flow back into build work silently. There is no detection of this condition.
findings.failure_mode: /implement and /run claim and 'implement' decision tickets from a map, contradicting the 'tickets cannot enter a sprint' guarantee in chart.md.
findings.suggested_fix: Use ((.issue_type // .type // "") | ascii_downcase) != "question" to match the other scripts, and add a bats case that feeds a fixture using the alternate field name.

findings.description: The new FR-1.1 exemption lets 'git branch -D spike/<slug>' through when grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml holds a decided row for the spike. The ledger is a tracked file the agent itself writes (dec-write-lib.sh, or directly), so the trust anchor for a destructive-command bypass is agent-controlled data, and the 'by: operator:*' transition is just a string in that file. The exemption also does not check that the local spike tip is actually on origin, although the SP-1 comment says a spike is 'pushed, never merged' and that is the only reason deletion is safe.
findings.failure_mode: A decided spike with unpushed local commits is force-deleted and the prototype is lost; or an agent forges/edits a decided row and removes the unmerged branch the hook was meant to protect.
findings.suggested_fix: Additionally require refs/remotes/origin/spike/<slug> to exist and equal the local tip (git rev-parse of both), and consider requiring the ledger file to be clean in git (no uncommitted modification) before trusting it.

findings.description: Slugs may contain '-', and both the dispatch cap (find -name ".chart-${SLUG}-*.dispatch") and the handoff report glob ("${RESEARCH}/chart-${SLUG}-"*.md) are prefix globs. Map 'eval' matches every marker and report of map 'eval-workers'.
findings.failure_mode: Map 'eval' hits the 5-dispatch cap because of 'eval-workers' research, and its hand-off snapshot inlines another map's research reports as settled context for /plan-and-analyze.
findings.suggested_fix: Encode a separator that cannot appear in a slug (e.g. 'chart-<slug>--<ticket>' or a per-map subdirectory grimoires/loa/research/<slug>/), or filter the matches against the map's known ticket slugs from map_rows.

findings.description: Only op_close --reason checks the dec-write-lib context. epic, ticket, resolve, rule-out and handoff can all be run unattended; the interactive-only rule depends on the skill prompt remembering to call chart-guard.sh first. The script already demonstrates the intended pattern for close, so the omission on the other write paths is inconsistent.
findings.failure_mode: An autonomous session charts a map and resolves its tickets itself, producing proposed rows and a hand-off snapshot that later reads as 'settled decisions; do not re-ask'.
findings.suggested_fix: Factor the context check from op_close into a helper and call it at the top of op_epic, op_ticket, op_resolve, op_rule_out and op_handoff (dry-run excepted if desired).

findings.description: The main-tree change detector is a before/after diff of git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching. For a directory ignored as a whole (typically .beads/, .run/), porcelain prints a single '!! dir/' entry regardless of its contents, so a probe that runs br (closing beads, claiming tickets) or writes run state is invisible. chart-ticket.sh research-end handles this case with a find -newer sweep of .run and .beads; the probe helper does not.
findings.failure_mode: An unblock probe mutates beads state or run-mode state in the main tree and the helper exits 0, reporting the tree unchanged.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same find -newer check over .beads and .run used in research-end (anchored on a timestamp file created before the probe), or snapshot checksums of those directories.
